about.title: Merced Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Merced's traffic runs mostly on a lettered-and-numbered street grid, and that is where its collisions concentrate. County public records for 2025 list 246 injury collisions in the city, 349 people hurt, and 3 traffic deaths. G Street, R Street, M Street, and W 16th Street account for the highest counts, and reports tend to cluster on Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. If one of those crashes was yours, the days afterward can feel scattered: a car in the shop, appointments to keep, and an adjuster asking for a recorded statement before you have had time to think. LawProactive exists to steady that moment. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Merced residents with an independent personal injury attorney who handles car accident claims on contingency, so nothing is owed unless there is a recovery. California allows two years to file in most cases, less when a public agency is involved, and the photos, receipts, and medical records you keep now will matter later.

whyChoose.title: Why Merced Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Deadlines are tracked from day one
items.desc: California gives most car accident claims two years, but if a city truck or county vehicle was involved, a claim may need to be filed in as little as six months. The attorney you are matched with knows which clock applies to your situation.

items.title: Partial fault does not close the door
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you share some blame, with the amount reduced by your percentage. There is also no cap on non-economic damages like pain and lost enjoyment of life.

items.title: Nothing out of pocket, and no pressure to talk to the other insurer
items.desc: Network attorneys work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. They also handle communication with the other driver's insurer so you are not pushed into a recorded statement you may later regret.

items.question: The other driver's insurer already called about my crash on R Street. Do I have to give them a recorded statement?
items.answer: No. You are not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company, and adjusters often ask for one early, before injuries have fully surfaced. It is reasonable to politely decline and let an attorney handle those conversations. In the meantime, keep your photos, the police report number, and any medical paperwork together in one place.

items.question: I think I was partly responsible. Can I still make a claim in Merced?
items.answer: Very likely yes. California uses pure comparative fault, so a claim is not barred just because you shared some of the blame. Your recovery would be reduced by your share of fault, but it is not eliminated. An attorney can look at the facts of your collision and explain how fault might be assigned.

items.question: How long do I have to file a car accident case in Merced County?
items.answer: Most California car accident claims must be filed within two years of the crash. That window shrinks dramatically, sometimes to six months, if a government entity such as the City of Merced or the county was involved. Because the deadline depends on who was at fault, it helps to speak with an attorney early rather than waiting.
